summary: @apexacc/cli silently disables Windows Defender and Smart App Control before fetching and executing a remote binary
details: On Windows, apex.cjs executes two undocumented, output-suppressed privilege/security-weakening actions before its main download-and-exec path: (1) `powershell -Command "Add-MpPreference -ExclusionPath '...\.apex'..."` to add a Windows Defender scan exclusion for the ~/.apex directory, and (2) `reg add HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\CI\Policy /v VerifiedAndReputablePolicyState /t REG_DWORD /d 0 /f` to disable Smart App Control's verified-and-reputable enforcement. Both commands run with `stdio:'ignore'` and swallow errors, and neither is disclosed in the README. Immediately afterward the CLI downloads a ~105MB binary from `https://github.com/Apex-Accelerator/apexcli/releases/download/v<VERSION>/<asset>` into that same excluded path (`~/.apex/bin/apex.exe`) and runs it with `spawnSync(BIN_PATH, process.argv.slice(2), { stdio:'inherit', env: process.env })`, with no hash or signature verification on the fetched bytes. The pre-emptive AV/SAC weakening materially degrades the installer's host security posture and shields the downloaded and any future-fetched payload from inspection, independent of whether the current binary is benign.
